name: SUSE S.A.
origin_detail: Founded 2 Sep 1992 in Nuremberg, Germany (Wikipedia infobox says Fuerth) by four founders as a Linux services/distribution company; holding company SUSE S.A. is registered in Luxembourg
openness_notes: Early SuSE Linux shipped GPL software but its key differentiator, the YaST installer/admin tool, was under a non-free licence that barred redistribution (to v9.0). Novell released YaST under the GPL in 2004 (SUSE 9.1). Today the whole portfolio is OSI-licensed and sold as subscriptions; in 2023 SUSE also funded an open RHEL-compatible fork via OpenELA.

license_history.license: GPL Linux distribution plus non-free YaST tool

license_history.note: Novell announced at BrainShare, 22 Mar 2004; effective with SUSE 9.1
SUSE pledged >$10M to fork RHEL, then co-founded OpenELA with Oracle and CIQ (10 Aug 2023)

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Opened SUSE's main differentiator after the Novell acquisition to attract outside developers; made YaST portable to other distributions

exit_events.note: Attachmate bought all of Novell for $2.2B (closed 27 Apr 2011); SUSE became a standalone unit; Attachmate merged into Micro Focus in 2014
Enterprise value $2.535B, announced 2 Jul 2018; closing date not verified in this pass
Priced at EUR 30/share in May 2021; market cap EUR 5.05B; ~EUR 1.1B of shares offered
EUR 16.00/share offer (Aug 2023), ~67% premium to last close but about half the IPO price; Reuters valued it at EUR 2.72B (Dow Jones EUR 2.83B incl. dividend); delisted

risk_events: Six ownership changes in 20 years (Novell 2004, Attachmate 2011, Micro Focus 2014, EQT 2019, Frankfurt IPO 2021, EQT take-private 2023)
2023: taken private at EUR 16/share, about half its EUR 30 IPO price two years earlier
Mar 2026: Reuters reported EQT exploring a sale (hired Arma Partners) at $4-6B
Nov 2026: ~10% job cuts (~190 people); CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen cited AI and automation
robustness: Commercially durable but financially passive: 34 years of continuous operation despite repeated sale between conglomerates and PE funds. All code is GPL/OSI and openSUSE is community-built, so the technology does not depend on SUSE's owner; revenue (~$780M FY2025) is a fraction of Red Hat's, and it returned to profit in FY2025.
physical_science_relevance: SUSE Linux Enterprise is common on HPC and supercomputer systems (e.g. HPE/Cray platforms) used in physical-science research.
openness_effect_assessment: SUSE opened its main proprietary differentiator (YaST) in 2004 without visible harm and today runs a fully open subscription model, but it never reached Red Hat's scale or pricing power; its value has swung with owners (EV $2.5B in 2018, EUR 5B at IPO, EUR 2.7B at take-private). In 2023 it used openness offensively, funding an open RHEL-compatible fork (OpenELA) when Red Hat restricted sources.
key_takeaway: SUSE shows that a fully open-source vendor can survive 30+ years and many owners because customers and the community depend on the code, not the cap table; but being the second open vendor in a market tends to yield modest growth, PE ownership, and periodic cost-cutting rather than a large standalone valuation.
